title: Measuring and Modeling Contractile Drying in Human Stratum Corneum
protocol: Mix 0.107 g of Sylgard 184 curing agent with 5.893 g base in a 20 mL glass vial.
Ensure homogeneity by mixing with a glass rod.
Place the glass vial in a vacuum chamber and degas to remove all bubbles.
Place a glass cover-slip (55 mm x 25 mm) in the center of a spin coater.
Add approximately 1 mL of the mixture onto the center of the cover-slip using a modified pipette.
Spin coat the cover-slip at 2,000 rpm for 60 seconds.
Repeat this process to create 5-6 substrates.
Cure the cover-slips in an oven for 12 hours at 60 °C.
Use a razor blade to partially remove the elastomer film from a sacrificial substrate.
Mark the topside of the elastomer film and the exposed glass with an indelible marker.
Mount the sample on an inverted microscope.
Record the difference in z-height between the focal planes of the two marks using a remote focus accessory.
This corresponds to the elastomer substrate thickness, h.
Heat a glass beaker half filled with deionized water to 60 °C in a water bath or heated stir plate.
Immerse the full thickness human skin in the heated water for 4 min inside a biological safety cabinet.
Transfer the skin sample into a beaker containing cooled deionized water (<10 °C) for 4 min.
Remove the skin from the beaker and place it in a Petri dish.
Gently isolate the epidermis using bent-nosed tissue tweezers.
Place the isolated epidermis basal side down on gauze-lined Petri dish.
Soak the gauze with trypsin solution (0.25% wt/vol type IX-S porcine pancreas in 0.1 M phosphate buffered saline).
Incubate for 6-8 h at room temperature to detach the stratum corneum (SC) from the epidermis.
Lift the gauze with tissue tweezers and float it in a container partially filled with deionized water.
Gently pull the SC to separate it from the gauze.
Wash the SC 3-4 times in deionized water to remove residual epidermal tissue.
Float the isolated SC in glycine max (soybean) trypsin inhibitor solution (0.4% in DW).
Agitate on a plate shaker for 10 min.
Place the SC in a Petri dish partially filled with deionized water and agitate on a plate shaker for 10 min.
Dry the isolated SC sheet on an ultra-fine plastic mesh for 48 h at room temperature (25 °C, 40% relative humidity).
Separate the SC from the mesh.
Cut out individual circular samples with a radius of 3 mm using a hole punch.
Mark the center of the outer face with a small spiral mark using an indelible marker.
Agitate SC samples for 30 minutes in 15 mL DW containing 90 µL fluorescent marker beads.
Remove SC samples and place them in a Petri dish partially filled with DW.
Partially immerse a substrate in the DW at a shallow angle of 15-30°.
Pin an edge of the floating SC sample at the contact line between the substrate and water interface.
Vertically withdraw the substrate from the water to laminate the SC sample to the substrate smoothly.
Repeat step 3.4 to place up to 6 SC samples onto each substrate.
Leave at least a 2-3 mm gap between samples.
Dry the mounted SC samples in laboratory conditions for 60 minutes.
Create a humidity chamber by placing a Petri dish partially filled with water into a hermetically sealed container.
Place substrates into the humidity chamber for 24 hours to equilibrate to a relative humidity of 99%.
Do not place the substrates directly into the Petri dish.
Mount the substrate on the microscope.
Place the perfusion chamber over the substrate.
Seal edges of the perfusion chamber to the elastomer using vacuum grease.
Equilibrate internal air to 99% R.H. prior to experimentation.
Reduce internal air humidity to desired value once imaging in sections 5 or 7 has begun.
Acquire images of SC samples using an inverted microscope with 1X objective lens.
Excite fluorescent beads using a light engine with FITC filter (503-530 nm emission bandpass).
Record fluorescent and transmitted light images using a digital CCD camera at a resolution of 1,392 x 1,040 pixels.
Take images with a frequency of 10 min for 16 h.
Place 1 mL silane (3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane; ≥98%) in some small plastic cap.
Place elastomer substrates from section 1 and the cap in a sealed container for 5 h.
Add 5 mg of EDC in a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 500 µL of DW to the EDC and agitate for 10 s using a vortex mixer.
Mix 0.076 g sodium tetraborate with 20 mL DW, then add 0.1 g boric acid and mix using a magnetic stirrer at 70 °C (1 h).
Add boric acid until the pH is 7.4.
Add 20 mL of borate buffer to a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 60 µL of 1 µm beads to the borate buffer.
Add 200 µL of EDC solution to bottle and mix thoroughly.
Pour bead solution into a 10 cm diameter Petri dish containing silanated substrates placed elastomer film-side down slowly.
Leave substrates in the bead solution for 45 min.
Use tweezers to remove substrates from the bead solution, then rinse with DW to remove unbound beads.
Air dry the substrates by blowing compressed air over the surface.
Seal the substrates in an opaque box to prevent photo-bleaching until SC sample deposition.
Deposit SC samples on to a substrate using section 3.
Apply a 5 µL drop of undiluted fluorescent marker bead solution (505/515 nm, 0.1 μm diameter) to the surface of each deposited SC sample with a pipette before completing step 3.6.
Establish measurements of SC thickness using the microscope with 40X objective lens.

Measure the thickness of SC samples over time using a remote focus accessory to record the difference in z-height between the two bead layer focal planes located at the SC-substrate interface and the topside of the SC.
Measure the thickness of 3 regions of each SC sample over a 3 h drying period.
Use particle image velocimetry to obtain spatially resolved in-plane drying displacements from the fluorescent images at each recorded time step.
Obtain azimuthally averaged radial and azimuthal displacement profiles from the displacement field of each radially symmetric SC sample using MATLAB.
Fit radial displacement profiles to a model describing drying SC as a shrinking linear elastic circular disk.
Assume the disk has time-varying thickness, hSC, radius R, and elastic modulus ESC.
Adhere the disk to a deformable elastic substrate with elastic modulus E.
Use Poisson's ratio νSC = 0.47 for the SC.
Obtain best fits using a minimum least squares approach.
Obtain model parameters α and β at each time step from the least squares fit of Equation (1) to the radial displacement profile.
Use fitting parameter β to obtain SC elastic modulus, ESC.
Use fitting parameter α to obtain the time varying contractile drying stress, PSC.
